To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformational and electrostatic properties of the three compounds are responsible for their differential action.
DHDMBFs are conformationally flexible and their conformations are stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions.

the conformational analysis and molecular modeling studies of 5-keto substituted 7-tertbutoxy-2,3 dihydro-3,3 dimethylbenzofuran analogs (1, 2, 4, 7) show that the conformation of 1 is more similar to that of the natural substrate arachidonic acid than the others, which may be the cause of its high COX-2 inhibitory activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new COX-2 selective inhibitors and their mechanism of action.
the development of new inhibitors of COX and LOX.
the development of a computational protocol to understand the conformational behavior of these molecules in the active cavity and their interaction with the peptide side chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformational and MEP distribution of the molecules are responsible for the selectivity of these molecules towards COX-2/5-LOX inhibition.
the conformation of these molecules is not the sole factor responsible for differential inhibition of COX-2 and LOX.

the 3-OH and 3-OMe substituted compounds are more flexible in the active cavity than the 3-Cl substituted one, the 3-OMet compound has a more favorable interaction with the active site residues than the 3-OHe and the 3- Cl substituted compounds and the 3-OEt substituted compound has the most favorable interaction with active site residues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DHDMBFs with 5-keto substituents have the potential of dual COX/LOX inhibition, but the conformational freedom and flexibility of the molecules are responsible for their selective action.
these molecules are conformationally flexible and the COX-2 inhibition is mainly due to the formation of H-bonds and pi-pi interactions between the molecules and amino acid residues of COX-2.
the 7-terbutyl-2,4-dioxo-3,3,6-trimethyl-2,3,3a,4-tetrahydropyrano[3,2-c]chromen-5-yl acetate (1) is a potent COX-2 inhibitor with a good selectivity for the COX-2/5-LOX.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conformational freedom of the molecules and its ability to make contacts with peptide side chain residues of the active cavity is the key factor for the selectivity of these molecules for COX-2 over COX-1 and 5-LOX.
the conformational rigidity of the 7-substituted benzofuran ring is the major cause of selectivity of these compounds.

the 5-keto group in these molecules plays a major role in determining their activity profile and that the 5-CH3 group of the 5-ketomethylene derivative (1a) is the most suitable group to interact with the COX-2 active cavity.
